Assert that conditions hold

Source: R/assert.R
assert.Rd

Check conditions on every row, like Stata's assert, and stop with the number of contradictions when any fails. It returns the data invisibly when all hold, so it can sit inside a pipeline.

Usage

assert(.data, ..., .by = NULL)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

Conditions evaluated like dplyr::mutate() expressions, each giving TRUE or FALSE per row (or a single value). Group functions such as n() and mean() use the groups of .data or .by.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping variables, like Stata's by g: assert.

Value

.data, invisibly, when every condition holds.

Details

The error lists each failing condition with its number of contradictions and the first failing rows. A missing result (NA) counts as a contradiction and is reported separately. This differs from Stata, where a missing value is larger than every number, so assert x > 0 holds when x is missing; write is.na(x) | x > 0 for that behaviour.

See also

Other data checking functions: is_first(), keys, stata_merge()

Examples

lifeexp |>
  assert(lexp > 0, popgrowth < 10) |>
  summ(lexp)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl      68     20    57  71.7  5.16    79

# Each country appears once per region
assert(lifeexp, dplyr::n() == dplyr::n_distinct(country), .by = region)

try(assert(lifeexp, safewater > 50))
#> Error in assert(lifeexp, safewater > 50) : Assertion failed:
#> • `safewater > 50`: 25 contradictions (14 missing) in 68 rows; rows 1, 4, 22,
#>   26, 29, ...
